meta.title: Ondra Reply Decision Log
meta.description: Records why she replied the way she did, append-only and read-only, for the interface and for audits (handbook §1.5, P1). Four decisions are fixed. First, it never enters the prompt: this record naturally carries counts, so injecting it would collide with the no-numbers rule and would turn "explaining herself" into a performance; there is no prompt outlet at all. Second, append only, never edit or delete: record() is the sole write entry, files are opened for append, and an audit log that can be edited is no longer an audit. Third, it never infers the reason: factors are handed in by the register chooser, emotion, the nine-step filter and the evidence gate; this package does not know what a factor means and only receives, masks, truncates, orders by weight and phrases it in plain Chinese. Inferring would put words in her mouth that nobody said. Fourth, no full text: only the short stretch she actually said (60 characters by default, can be turned off) plus structured factors; user messages, memory bodies and prompts are never stored. Storage is one JSONL per day, and a corrupt line is skipped without affecting the rest. Retention applies only when pruning is called explicitly, with no timer, because automatic deletion is asymmetric: deleting wrongly loses the only clue for good. This package registers no tools, runs no timers, makes no network requests and draws no interface: the log view, filters and timeline belong to the app shell.
